text: Noticing a large mug of mead on the table. <break time="0.8s" /> The newcomer drank from it. <break time="0.8s" /> So deeply and so often. <break time="0.8s" /> That Missus Fennel watched him. <break time="0.8s" /> With growing alarm. <break time="0.8s" /> When the guests asked about his trade. <break time="0.8s" /> He answered with a mysterious smile. <break time="0.8s" /> That he was going to Casterbridge. <break time="0.8s" /> On business of a very special kind. <break time="0.8s" /> Then, instead of explaining. <break time="0.8s" /> He began to sing a strange song. <break time="0.8s" /> Whose verses were like riddles. <break time="0.8s" /> Telling of a trade that was the rarest one of all. <break time="0.8s" /> He sang that he tied his customers up. <break time="0.8s" /> And took them up on high. <break time="0.8s" /> And then sent them away. <break time="0.8s" /> To a far country. <break time="0.8s" /> All in a cheerful voice. <break time="0.8s" /> At first the guests could not guess the meaning. <break time="0.8s" /> But slowly, one by one. <break time="0.8s" /> They understood. <break time="0.8s" /> And the room fell into a frightened silence. <break time="0.8s" /> The man in gray was the hangman. <break time="0.8s" /> On his way to Casterbridge Jail. <break time="0.8s" /> Where a prisoner was to be executed. <break time="0.8s" /> The next morning. <break time="0.8s" /> For stealing a sheep. <break time="0.8s" /> Everyone had heard of the poor clockmaker. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had stolen the sheep in broad daylight. <break time="0.8s" /> Because his wife and children were starving. <break time="0.8s" /> Strangely the first stranger. <break time="0.8s" /> Still sitting by the fire. <break time="0.8s" /> Joined loudly in the chorus of the song. <break time="0.8s" /> As if nothing in the world troubled him.
